skill.name: TF-IDF Term Weighting Theory Reference
skill.description: Canonical knowledge reference documenting the historical and theoretical foundations of term frequency-inverse document frequency (tf-idf) weighting schemes in information retrieval. Traces intellectual lineage from Luhn (1957) through modern probabilistic language models, enabling practitioners to understand, justify, and select appropriate tf-idf variants and related weighting approaches.
skill.skill_body:
When implementing, reviewing, or justifying term weighting schemes in information retrieval systems, consult this reference to trace the intellectual history and theoretical foundations of tf-idf. Use this to understand why inverse document frequency matters, how tf-idf evolved, and what alternatives exist.

## Objective

document_weighting_theory
## Applicable Signals

- implementing or understanding tf-idf variants
- reviewing term weighting history
- justifying weighting scheme selection
- designing custom term weighting functions
- evaluating alternative weighting approaches

## Contraindications

- real-time query execution or immediate scoring computation needed
- operational deployment requiring only implementation code without theoretical justification
- time-critical retrieval tasks where reference lookup is infeasible

## Workflow Steps

- Identify the weighting scheme under consideration or being designed
- Consult foundational papers by Luhn, Spärck Jones, Salton & Buckley to understand core concepts
- Review extensions and theoretical justifications (Robertson & Jones, Croft & Harper, Papineni)
- Examine SMART notation and exhaustive weighting function spaces (Moffat & Zobel)
- Document rationale for scheme selection or variant choice

## Constraints

- This is reference material only; does not provide executable weighting algorithms or implementation code
- Citations are historical; some early papers may require archival access or institutional library access
- Does not substitute for empirical evaluation of weighting schemes on specific collections

## Cautions

- Hill-climbing optimization of weighting schemes may not converge to best combinations (Moffat & Zobel 1998)
- Probabilistic language models (Chapter 11) offer more nuanced weighting than tf-idf for some applications

## Output Contract

- Practitioner can cite and explain foundational papers: Luhn (1957, 1958) on medium-frequency term importance; Spärck Jones (1972) on inverse document frequency; Salton & Buckley (1987) on theoretical justifications
- Practitioner can articulate the rationale for tf-idf weighting scheme selection and justify variant choices
- Practitioner can reference extensions and alternatives: Robertson & Jones (1976), Croft & Harper (1979), Papineni (2001) on idf extensions; Singhal et al. (1996a) on pivoted document length normalization; probabilistic language models as alternatives
- Practitioner understands SMART notation and exhaustive weighting function spaces for term and document frequency weighting
